searchText: https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth2/blob/0bae91b79565364c10e8267fadc7dd8cc1517296/docs/e2store.md#era-files - some notes about an import/export format for blocks and states - for example, it's fairly nifty to have files like these around when dealing with weak subjectivity sync - they could also be circulated with out-of-band techniques and used for multi-block test cases - some stats in the PR: https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth2/pull/2382 - planning to post to eth2 repo at some point (per earlier discussions) but early comments welcome! tldr; an era file contains 8192 blocks and one state, for a total of around 60-70mb, 10 of which is the state itself (snappy-compressed) - 8192 matches the number of block roots in that state, meaning the blocks can be verified and trust needs only to be established for the state sadly, the historical roots in states mix both state and block roots in the same top-level hash - if they were separate, it would be easier to blocks from distant past using historical roots from a recent state the grand total so far that we've generated for mainnet is about 3gb of blocks and 500:ish mb of states, when storing one state per 8192 blocks (snappy-compressed) oh nice. this might serve as a good EIP/erc
